title: VoltRide E-Bike Battery Fire Incident Reports
premise: Several users of a budget e-bike reported battery fires while charging.

side_A.role: an advocate at a consumer-safety group
side_A.goal: pushing for a recall of the product

side_B.goal: showing the product is safe when used as directed

=== DOCUMENT 1: VoltRide Corporate Records and Product Specifications ===

VoltRide, Inc.
Principal Executive Office: 4500 Commerce Boulevard, Suite 200, Austin, Texas 78745
Incorporated: Delaware

PRODUCT SPECIFICATION SHEET — MODEL C-7 ELECTRIC BICYCLE
Launch Date: January 15, 2022

VoltRide launched the Model C-7 on January 15, 2022 with a press release highlighting its 40-mile range per charge. The Model C-7 retails at $899, making it one of the five lowest-priced e-bikes in its frame class. VoltRide has sold approximately 42,000 Model C-7 e-bikes in North America between January 2022 and November 2023.

BATTERY SPECIFICATIONS
- Type: Lithium-ion
- Voltage: 36 volts
- Capacity: 10.4 amp-hours
- Weight: 6.2 pounds
- Warranty: 12-month limited warranty with specific exclusions for damage from aftermarket chargers

CHARGER SPECIFICATIONS
- AC Input: 100-240V
- DC Output: 42V at 2.0 amps
- Weight: 1.1 pounds

USER MANUAL SAFETY WARNINGS
The Model C-7 user manual includes 18 separate safety warnings regarding charging, covering outlet selection, ambient temperature, and charging intervals.

BATTERY SUPPLIER CERTIFICATIONS
VoltRide's battery supplier, CellTech Industries of Shenzhen, China, holds ISO 9001 and UN38.3 certifications for its lithium-ion battery packs.

QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM
VoltRide's quality assurance program includes a 72-hour burn-in test on 5% of randomly sampled battery packs from each production lot before shipment.

CUSTOMER SUPPORT OPERATIONS
VoltRide maintains a customer support call center in Austin, Texas staffed by 34 representatives operating 7 days a week. VoltRide has responded to 312 customer inquiries regarding battery performance through its online portal since January 2023, with an average response time of 4.5 hours.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement of Angela Torres ===

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Angela Torres
Address: [Redacted], Dayton, Ohio
Date of Statement: May 3, 2023

My name is Angela Torres. I purchased a VoltRide Model C-7 electric bicycle in January 2023 from a retailer in Dayton. I kept the e-bike in my garage and regularly charged it overnight.

On March 14, 2023, my Model C-7 battery ignited at 2:15 a.m. while plugged into a wall outlet in my garage. I was awakened by a loud popping sound and discovered flames coming from the area where the e-bike was charging. I called 911 and the Dayton Fire Department responded. The fire caused damage to my garage and destroyed the e-bike.

Regarding the charger I used: I exclusively used the grey charger that came in the Model C-7 box from the day I purchased it and never purchased or used any other charger. I still have the original box the e-bike came in, and the charger compartment was empty after the fire because the charger was the one plugged into the wall when the fire started.

Regarding communications with VoltRide: On April 10, 2023 a VoltRide representative called me and offered $5,000 and a replacement e-bike if I signed a confidentiality agreement and withdrew my CPSC complaint. I did not accept the offer. The caller identified himself as a customer support supervisor named Derek Halverson.

I signed and submitted a complaint to the CPSC describing the incident.

---

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statement of Derek Halverson ===

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Derek Halverson
Title: Customer Support Supervisor, VoltRide, Inc.
Location: Austin, Texas Customer Support Center
Date of Statement: May 10, 2023

I am employed as a Customer Support Supervisor at VoltRide's call center in Austin, Texas, which is staffed by 34 representatives operating 7 days a week. I have held this position since November 2022.

Regarding the Torres incident charger: Photographs of the charger recovered from the Torres garage show a black third-party charger inconsistent with any unit VoltRide has ever shipped. The Model C-7 battery charger is rated for 100-240V AC input and outputs 42V DC at 2.0 amps, weighing 1.1 pounds, and is grey in color. The charger depicted in the photographs taken by the Dayton Fire Department does not match this description. The Model C-7 battery pack carries a 12-month limited warranty with specific exclusions for damage from aftermarket chargers.

Regarding prior fire complaints: No complaints mentioning fire, smoke, overheating, or thermal events appear anywhere in VoltRide's customer support database prior to March 14, 2023. VoltRide has responded to 312 customer inquiries regarding battery performance through its online portal since January 2023, with an average response time of 4.5 hours. None of these inquiries referenced fire, smoke, or thermal events prior to the Torres incident.

Regarding settlement offers to Angela Torres: VoltRide has never offered Angela Torres any monetary settlement, replacement product, or confidentiality agreement of any kind. I did contact Ms. Torres by telephone on April 10, 2023, but the purpose of the call was to gather information about the incident for our internal investigation and to remind her of the warranty exclusions for damage caused by aftermarket chargers. No offer of compensation or confidentiality was discussed during that call or any other communication.

---

=== DOCUMENT 5: Witness Statements of SafeRide USA and VoltRide Technical Experts ===

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Lena Vasquez
Title: Lead Investigator, SafeRide USA
Date of Statement: May 15, 2023

I serve as Lead Investigator for SafeRide USA, a consumer advocacy organization. SafeRide USA has catalogued 11 fire-related complaints involving Model C-7 e-bikes between February 2023 and October 2023. On September 22, 2023, Patricia Nguyen of Portland, Oregon submitted photographs of a charred Model C-7 battery to SafeRide USA. Portland Fire Bureau report PF-2023-8891 lists the cause of the Nguyen residence fire as "undetermined" with a Model C-7 battery noted as a potential ignition source.

Regarding prior complaints known to VoltRide: A former VoltRide support representative told me the company had logged at least two battery overheating complaints from Model C-7 owners before March 14, 2023. The representative, whose identity I am preserving as a confidential source, stated that these complaints were received through VoltRide's customer support call center in Austin, Texas in late 2022 and early 2023. The representative indicated that the complaints were entered into the company's customer support database but were classified under general performance inquiries rather than safety reports.

SafeRide USA is continuing to investigate the full scope of Model C-7 battery incidents and is coordinating with consumers who have filed reports with the CPSC.

---

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Dr. Raymond Okafor
Title: Battery Safety Consultant
Retained by: SafeRide USA
Date of Statement: May 20, 2023

I am a battery safety consultant with expertise in lithium-ion battery systems. I was retained by SafeRide USA to conduct independent testing of the VoltRide Model C-7 battery pack.

The Model C-7 uses a 36-volt, 10.4-amp-hour lithium-ion battery pack weighing 6.2 pounds. VoltRide's battery supplier, CellTech Industries of Shenzhen, China, holds ISO 9001 and UN38.3 certifications for its lithium-ion battery packs. VoltRide's quality assurance program includes a 72-hour burn-in test on 5% of randomly sampled battery packs from each production lot before shipment.

Regarding the battery management system thermal cutoff: My testing of three Model C-7 battery packs shows the thermal cutoff activates only at 87°C, which is 17 degrees above the safe threshold for this cell chemistry. Testing was conducted in a controlled laboratory environment using calibrated thermal sensors applied directly to the battery cells. All three packs exhibited thermal cutoff activation at or above 85°C, with the average activation temperature recorded at 87°C. This threshold is above the manufacturer-stated safe operating range for the cell chemistry used in these packs.

---

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Dr. Megan Pruitt
Title: Director of Product Safety, VoltRide, Inc.
Date of Statement: May 22, 2023

I serve as Director of Product Safety at VoltRide, Inc., which is incorporated in Delaware with its principal executive office located at 4500 Commerce Boulevard, Suite 200, Austin, Texas 78745. VoltRide launched the Model C-7 on January 15, 2022 with a press release highlighting its 40-mile range per charge. VoltRide has sold approximately 42,000 Model C-7 e-bikes in North America between January 2022 and November 2023.

Regarding the battery management system thermal cutoff: Our production-line testing confirms the thermal cutoff on every Model C-7 battery pack activates between 65°C and 68°C, well within the safe operating range for this cell chemistry. This testing is conducted as part of VoltRide's quality assurance program, which includes a 72-hour burn-in test on 5% of randomly sampled battery packs from each production lot before shipment. The thermal cutoff values recorded during production-line testing are documented in batch quality records and are consistent with the specifications provided by CellTech Industries, our battery supplier, which holds ISO 9001 and UN38.3 certifications for its lithium-ion battery packs.

The Model C-7 user manual includes 18 separate safety warnings regarding charging, covering outlet selection, ambient temperature, and charging intervals. These warnings are designed to ensure that consumers operate the battery and charger within safe parameters.
